themes.theme: constraintSummary's null-report guard (model.ts) and QualityPanel's rendering of that guard are two independently-unverified layers of the same 'must never render as satisfied' promise — a string constructed at the model layer and consumed at the DOM layer with no test pinning either end or the seam between them
findingSummaries: `constraintSummary` is referenced by zero tests at any level; its documented 'a null report must never render as satisfied' guarantee is unenforced, and inverting it passes the whole suite (model.ts).

No test in the suite renders QualityPanel, so the gauge, the connection caption and both shortfall disclosures — all downstream of constraintSummary and its siblings — are pinned only at the model layer and their wiring to the DOM is unguarded (QualityPanel.tsx); the finding text itself names QualityPanel as the 'sibling' gap of the constraintSummary gap.
themes.remediation: Tighten constraintSummary's `report === null` branch to return one explicit sentinel value (rather than a prose string downstream code matches by keyword) and make QualityPanel's satisfaction rendering key off that sentinel exclusively — collapsing the current two independently-unguarded obligations (model.ts's string construction and QualityPanel's consumption of it) into a single boundary check instead of leaving both unverified.

themes.theme: model.ts's inline field comments (on `report` and `girth`) describe usage that has already drifted or is about to drift from what the code actually does, with no mechanism forcing the comment to track the code
findingSummaries: Landing the already-scoped buildReport-on-import follow-on makes model.ts:130's `report === null` branch dead and the comment at model.ts:122-123 ('an imported constrained file has no report') false; verified by performing the wiring and tracing that report is null in only one unrelated case (model.ts).
Girth comment in model.ts understates M3 usage: it says girth is not displayed, but it is now used to derive `separationShortfall` shown in QualityPanel (model.ts).
themes.remediation: Delete the free-form prose comments on the `report` and `girth` fields in model.ts (the 'saved with this graph — not re-checked on import' text and the 'not displayed' text) instead of maintaining separate documentation that can silently fall out of sync with actual consumers — let the field declarations stand alone, with the field's real usage (constraintSummary, separationShortfall) as the only source of truth.

themes.theme: shortestPath is a direction-dependent primitive, and the lower-index canonicalisation that makes usePathFinder draw a symmetric route for (s,t) vs (t,s) is an untested, deletable invariant
findingSummaries: `shortestPath` returns different (equally short) routes for (s,t) and (t,s); the lower-index canonicalisation that makes 'Ana then Ben' draw the same line as 'Ben then Ana' is deleteable with the whole suite green (usePathFinder.ts).
themes.remediation: Tighten shortestPath itself to always canonicalise (lower-index first) internally before searching, and delete the separate post-hoc reorientation step in usePathFinder — unifying the forward and reverse query call sites onto one code path removes the untested asymmetry instead of adding a test to guard it.

themes.theme: neighborhood.ts's chip-bucket projection (relatedChips) and its '+N more' counter independently decide what counts as shown vs hidden, so the two can silently disagree or double-count without any test noticing
findingSummaries: Two membership/counting properties of neighborhood/relatedChips that PersonPanel renders directly are unpinned — focus-exclusion and shown+hidden-equals-total — and both mutations pass the suite (neighborhood.ts).
themes.remediation: Delete relatedChips' own slicing/counting logic and have it call the existing clampList boundary check directly, so there is exactly one place that decides the shown/hidden split instead of two independently-maintained boundary checks that can drift apart.

themes.theme: a defensive clamp in App.tsx is justified by a causal story (async ordering vs resetSelection) that cannot be reproduced, so the comment asserts a hazard the code's own structure appears to exclude
findingSummaries: The comment above the `selected` range clamp in App.tsx claims a selection can survive into a shorter replacement view because resetSelection runs before the asynchronous bg.generate; this window could not be reproduced, and deleting the clamp passes the suite.
themes.remediation: Delete the unreproducible causal claim from the App.tsx comment rather than keeping a justification nobody can reconstruct; the real defense is eccentricity's own vertex guard downstream, so state only that dependency — removing the false narrative instead of adding a test to validate it.

themes.theme: the connection-quality gauge's only explanation of what its number means lives solely in a mouse-hover `title` attribute on a non-focusable div, so keyboard/screen-reader users get a bare, unit-less digit disconnected from the adjacent caption text that could have carried the explanation
findingSummaries: QualityPanel's gauge explanation ('how close to the theoretical best...') is only in a `title` attribute on a non-focusable div; the visible number has no '%' unit, and connectionSummary's adjacent text never restates the number or the word 'quality'/'percent', so the number and its meaning are never connected for non-mouse users.
themes.remediation: Remove the split between the hidden tooltip and the separate caption — fold the gauge's meaning directly into the existing connectionSummary text so there is one accessible text channel instead of two disconnected ones, rather than bolting on a new aria-label element alongside the tooltip.

gating.theme: the only sentence that tells the organizer whether their buddy rules were honored is verified by nothing, so "not measured" can silently become "satisfied"
gating.summary: `constraintSummary` is referenced by zero tests at any level; its documented "a null report must never render as satisfied" guarantee is unenforced, and inverting it passes the whole suite.
gating.failure: Seeded mutation: change `model.ts:130` from ``if (report === null) return `${rules} saved with this graph — not re-checked on import.`;`` to ``if (report === null) return `all ${rules} satisfied`;``. `npm test` → 315 passed. Reachable input: import any exported file carrying buddy rules (`importGraph` sets `report: null` because no builder ran) → QualityPanel would tell the organizer all N rules were honored when nothing checked a single edge. Two further mutations are also green: dropping the `broken === 0` guard (`return "all N satisfied"` whatever the violation counts), and making `constraintSummary` return `null` always (the rules line vanishes from the panel). `grep -rn constraintSummary app/test/` returns nothing; `importExport.roundtrip.test.ts:382` pins `view.report === null`, i.e. the field, not the string derived from it.
gating.remediation: Add a test over `constraintSummary` covering all three branches by their OUTPUT string, not the field: (a) `report === null` with `constraints.length > 0` must not match /satisfied/; (b) a report with `reqViolations + prohViolations > 0` must not match /satisfied/; (c) `constraints.length === 0` returns null. Assert (a) through the real import path (`importGraph(exportGraph(constrainedView))`) so the seam, not just the function, is pinned. Name the sibling in the same commit: `QualityPanel` is where the string is rendered and has no render test either (filed separately).
gating.invariant: For every GraphView v, `/satisfied/.test(constraintSummary(v) ?? "") === (v.report !== null && v.report.reqViolations + v.report.prohViolations === 0 && v.constraints.length > 0)` — i.e. the word "satisfied" appears if and only if a report exists AND counts zero violations.

gating.theme: a path is reconstructed from a direction-dependent core primitive, and the tie-break that makes the drawn chain symmetric is load-bearing but untested
gating.summary: `shortestPath` returns different (equally short) routes for (s,t) and (t,s); the lower-index canonicalisation that makes "Ana then Ben" draw the same line as "Ben then Ana" is deleteable with the whole suite green.
gating.failure: Measured: on four app-generated graphs (n=12/k=3, 16/3, 20/4, 30/4, seed 12345) there are 98 pairs where `shortestPath(g,s,t)` reversed !== `shortestPath(g,t,s)` — e.g. n=12 k=3, 1↔10 gives [1,2,8,10] one way and [1,6,0,10] the other. Seeded mutation `const [s, t] = [source, target];` (dropping the canonicalisation at line 22): `npm test` → 315 passed. With it removed, picking two people in the opposite order lights a different chain in the graph, in PathPanel's chips, and in the always-mounted `sr-live` region, with the same step count — the docstring's stated contract, unenforced.
gating.remediation: Add a property test over `usePathFinder` (or its pure core: canonicalise → `shortestPath` → orient) that, for a generated graph and every reachable pair, the route for (a,b) is the exact reverse of the route for (b,a) and `route[0] === source`. Quantify over all pairs of one real graph rather than listing pairs, since the asymmetry is data-dependent.
gating.invariant: For every graph g and all a ≠ b in [0,g.n): with source=a,target=b the resolved route R1 and with source=b,target=a the resolved route R2 satisfy `R1 === null ? R2 === null : (R1[0] === a && R2[0] === b && R1.join() === [...R2].reverse().join())`.

gating.theme: the explorer card's chip projection and its "+N more" counter can disagree with each other, or list a person as two steps from themselves, without any test noticing
gating.summary: Two membership/counting properties of `neighborhood`/`relatedChips` that PersonPanel renders directly are unpinned; both mutations pass the suite.
gating.failure: Seeded mutations, each green across 315 tests: (1) drop `c !== focus` at `neighborhood.ts:22` — the focused person enters `second`, so PersonPanel renders them as their own "Two steps away" chip and `isShownRelated(adj, i, i)` becomes true, changing the back-stack trail rule; (2) `all.slice(0, SECOND_LIMIT)` → `all.slice(0, SECOND_LIMIT + 1)` at `neighborhood.ts:51` — 25 chips render while `secondHidden` still counts `length - 24`, so one person is both shown and counted in "+N more" and the displayed count is off by one. Second-degree sets reach 132 at the degree cap, so the cutoff is live, not theoretical. A related boundary in the same class: `clamp.ts:54` `items.length <= limit` → `<` also survives, which would make a person with exactly 12 buddies announce as "…, and 0 more" through `selectionStatusText`.
gating.remediation: Pin the projection's two structural properties over a generated graph and every focus index: focus is in neither bucket, the buckets are disjoint, and shown + hidden equals the full two-step count. Add the `clampList` equality boundary (`items.length === limit` renders no "and N more") in the same commit — same theme, one delimiter over.
gating.invariant: For every adjacency and every focus i: `!first.has(i) && !second.has(i)`, `first` and `second` are disjoint, and `relatedChips(adj,i).secondShown.length + relatedChips(adj,i).secondHidden === neighborhood(adj,i).second.size`; and for all items/limit, `clampList(items, limit)` contains "and 0 more" for no input.

gating.summary: Implementing the follow-on this project has actually committed to (re-check buddy rules on import, using the core's own buildReport rather than a hand-rolled copy of the satisfaction predicate — exactly as prescribed in app/CLAUDE.md's 'Known follow-ons') makes model.ts:130's `report === null` branch dead in the live call graph, and turns the comment at model.ts:122-123 ('an imported constrained file has no report') false. I verified this by actually performing the wiring: after the fix, GraphView.report is null in exactly two situations — fromUnconstrained() in worker/generate.ts (reached only when there are zero constraints, so QualityPanel's `constraintSummary` already short-circuits on `total === 0` before ever reading `report`) and nowhere else, since fromConstrained() and the fixed importGraph.ts both always populate `report` whenever constraints exist. That leaves `constraintSummary`'s 'saved with this graph — not re-checked on import' string, and the comment explaining it, permanently unreachable from real data.
gating.failure: Import a file with constraints (e.g. `{required:[[0,1]]}`) after the fix and read the quality panel: it now correctly says 'all 1 buddy rule satisfied' (a genuine improvement), but model.ts:122-123's comment still claims imported files have no report, and the dead `report === null` branch/string remain, so a future reader trusts a comment the fix itself invalidated.
gating.remediation: When landing the buildReport wiring (importGraph.ts + lib export), remove or rewrite model.ts:119-134's comment and the now-unreachable `report === null` branch in the same commit, rather than leaving it to a later comment sweep — the fan-out for this follow-on is three files (lib/src/core/index.ts, app/src/io/importGraph.ts, app/src/model.ts), not the two the follow-on note names.
gating.invariant: for every GraphView v with v.constraints.length > 0 that is reachable from a real code path (generation or import), v.report !== null — i.e. `report === null && constraints.length > 0` is unreachable, so any UI string/comment keyed on that condition is dead and must not exist

gating.summary: Girth comment understates M3 usage: it is now displayed via separationShortfall.
gating.failure: Line 67 states: 'girth: number | null; // export-only (meta.metrics); not displayed in M2; null for a forest'. The girth value is the ONLY source of truth for separation reporting (postulate: separation = girth - 1 per the core's own definition).

gating.theme: a value's meaning is explained only through a pointer-hover mechanism, so a keyboard/screen-reader user reading the quality numbers gets a bare, unit-less digit with no way to learn what it measures
gating.summary:
The connection-quality gauge's only explanation of what its number means ('how close to the theoretical best (Moore bound) this graph is. Zero when the group is split into disconnected sub-groups.') lives entirely in a `title` attribute on a non-focusable `
`. `title` is a mouse-hover tooltip; it is not exposed to keyboard users (the div has no `tabIndex`, so it can never receive focus and browsers generally do not surface `title` outside of a mouse hover/focus event) and most screen readers do not read `title` on non-interactive, unfocused elements at all. The visible number itself (`
{q}
`) carries no unit either — no '%' character in the markup — so a screen reader lands on a bare integer with no indication it is a percentage or what it is a percentage of; the adjacent `connectionSummary` text ('everyone's well-linked for 4 buddies each' / 'not enough people yet to score') never restates the number or the word 'quality'/'percent', so the number and its explanation are never connected for anyone not sighted enough to read the tooltip.
gating.failure: A screen-reader user tabbing (or reading in document order with the screen off) through the metrics band after generating a graph hears, for the quality metric: the digits (e.g. '82') then 'everyone's well-linked for 4 buddies each' — with no announcement anywhere of the word 'percent', 'quality', or the Moore-bound explanation a sighted user can get by hovering the gauge. Contrast with the two neighboring metrics on the same panel, `aspl` and `diameter`, each of which pairs its number with an explicit label ('avg hops between any two people', 'most steps between anyone') in the accessible tree.
gating.remediation: Move the explanatory sentence (or a shorter equivalent, e.g. `${q}% connection quality — how close to the theoretical best for this many buddies`) into an `aria-label` on the `.gauge` div (or a visually-hidden text node inside it) so it is present in the accessible tree unconditionally, the same way `aspl`/`diameter` already pair their digits with a text label; keep `title` for the mouse tooltip if desired, but don't make it the only channel.
gating.invariant: Every piece of information exposed via a `title` attribute on a non-focusable element must also be reachable via the accessible name, accessible description, or an adjacent static/live text node of that element — i.e. no user-facing explanation should be reachable by pointer hover alone.

Seeded mutation `const [s, t] = [source, target];` (dropping the canonicalisation at line 22): `npm test` → 315 passed. With it removed, picking two people in the opposite order lights a different chain in the graph, in PathPanel's chips, and in the always-mounted `sr-live` region, with the same step count — the docstring's stated contract, unenforced.
confirmed.remediation: Add a property test over `usePathFinder` (or its pure core: canonicalise → `shortestPath` → orient) that, for a generated graph and every reachable pair, the route for (a,b) is the exact reverse of the route for (b,a) and `route[0] === source`. Quantify over all pairs of one real graph rather than listing pairs, since the asymmetry is data-dependent.
confirmed.invariant: For every graph g and all a ≠ b in [0,g.n): with source=a,target=b the resolved route R1 and with source=b,target=a the resolved route R2 satisfy `R1 === null ? R2 === null : (R1[0] === a && R2[0] === b && R1.join() === [...R2].reverse().join())`.

confirmed.theme: the explorer card's chip projection and its "+N more" counter can disagree with each other, or list a person as two steps from themselves, without any test noticing
confirmed.summary: Two membership/counting properties of `neighborhood`/`relatedChips` that PersonPanel renders directly are unpinned; both mutations pass the suite.
confirmed.failure: Seeded mutations, each green across 315 tests: (1) drop `c !== focus` at `neighborhood.ts:22` — the focused person enters `second`, so PersonPanel renders them as their own "Two steps away" chip and `isShownRelated(adj, i, i)` becomes true, changing the back-stack trail rule; (2) `all.slice(0, SECOND_LIMIT)` → `all.slice(0, SECOND_LIMIT + 1)` at `neighborhood.ts:51` — 25 chips render while `secondHidden` still counts `length - 24`, so one person is both shown and counted in "+N more" and the displayed count is off by one. Second-degree sets reach 132 at the degree cap, so the cutoff is live, not theoretical. A related boundary in the same class: `clamp.ts:54` `items.length <= limit` → `<` also survives, which would make a person with exactly 12 buddies announce as "…, and 0 more" through `selectionStatusText`.
confirmed.remediation: Pin the projection's two structural properties over a generated graph and every focus index: focus is in neither bucket, the buckets are disjoint, and shown + hidden equals the full two-step count. Add the `clampList` equality boundary (`items.length === limit` renders no "and N more") in the same commit — same theme, one delimiter over.
confirmed.invariant: For every adjacency and every focus i: `!first.has(i) && !second.has(i)`, `first` and `second` are disjoint, and `relatedChips(adj,i).secondShown.length + relatedChips(adj,i).secondHidden === neighborhood(adj,i).second.size`; and for all items/limit, `clampList(items, limit)` contains "and 0 more" for no input.

confirmed.theme: the fact 'report is null on the import path' is asserted independently in two files (importGraph.ts's construction and model.ts's consumption) with no shared symbol tying them together, so fixing the producer silently strands the consumer's comment and copy
confirmed.summary: Implementing the follow-on this project has actually committed to (re-check buddy rules on import, using the core's own buildReport rather than a hand-rolled copy of the satisfaction predicate — exactly as prescribed in app/CLAUDE.md's 'Known follow-ons') makes model.ts:130's `report === null` branch dead in the live call graph, and turns the comment at model.ts:122-123 ('an imported constrained file has no report') false. I verified this by actually performing the wiring: after the fix, GraphView.report is null in exactly two situations — fromUnconstrained() in worker/generate.ts (reached only when there are zero constraints, so QualityPanel's `constraintSummary` already short-circuits on `total === 0` before ever reading `report`) and nowhere else, since fromConstrained() and the fixed importGraph.ts both always populate `report` whenever constraints exist. That leaves `constraintSummary`'s 'saved with this graph — not re-checked on import' string, and the comment explaining it, permanently unreachable from real data.
confirmed.failure: Import a file with constraints (e.g. `{required:[[0,1]]}`) after the fix and read the quality panel: it now correctly says 'all 1 buddy rule satisfied' (a genuine improvement), but model.ts:122-123's comment still claims imported files have no report, and the dead `report === null` branch/string remain, so a future reader trusts a comment the fix itself invalidated.
confirmed.remediation: When landing the buildReport wiring (importGraph.ts + lib export), remove or rewrite model.ts:119-134's comment and the now-unreachable `report === null` branch in the same commit, rather than leaving it to a later comment sweep — the fan-out for this follow-on is three files (lib/src/core/index.ts, app/src/io/importGraph.ts, app/src/model.ts), not the two the follow-on note names.
confirmed.invariant: for every GraphView v with v.constraints.length > 0 that is reachable from a real code path (generation or import), v.report !== null — i.e. `report === null && constraints.length > 0` is unreachable, so any UI string/comment keyed on that condition is dead and must not exist

confirmed.theme: comment claims girth is not displayed when it is now used to derive displayed separation information
confirmed.summary: Girth comment understates M3 usage: it is now displayed via separationShortfall.
confirmed.failure: Line 67 states: 'girth: number | null; // export-only (meta.metrics); not displayed in M2; null for a forest'. However, girth IS now displayed in M3: the separationShortfall() function (lines 255–263) derives the displayed separation value directly from girth (got = girth - 1), and QualityPanel (lines 53–57 in QualityPanel.tsx) displays this shortfall to the user.
confirmed.remediation: Update the comment to reflect M3 usage: 'girth: number | null; // derived to show minimum-separation shortfall in QualityPanel; null for a forest'. Alternatively, remove the version reference entirely and state only the current usage.
confirmed.invariant: For any graph view where girth !== null and constraints.length === 0, separationShortfall must return a non-null result when got < asked, and this result must be rendered in the UI. The girth value is the ONLY source of truth for separation reporting (postulate: separation = girth - 1 per the core's own definition).

confirmed.theme: a value's meaning is explained only through a pointer-hover mechanism, so a keyboard/screen-reader user reading the quality numbers gets a bare, unit-less digit with no way to learn what it measures
confirmed.summary:
The connection-quality gauge's only explanation of what its number means ('how close to the theoretical best (Moore bound) this graph is. Zero when the group is split into disconnected sub-groups.') lives entirely in a `title` attribute on a non-focusable `
`. `title` is a mouse-hover tooltip; it is not exposed to keyboard users (the div has no `tabIndex`, so it can never receive focus and browsers generally do not surface `title` outside of a mouse hover/focus event) and most screen readers do not read `title` on non-interactive, unfocused elements at all. The visible number itself (`
{q}
`) carries no unit either — no '%' character in the markup — so a screen reader lands on a bare integer with no indication it is a percentage or what it is a percentage of; the adjacent `connectionSummary` text ('everyone's well-linked for 4 buddies each' / 'not enough people yet to score') never restates the number or the word 'quality'/'percent', so the number and its explanation are never connected for anyone not sighted enough to read the tooltip.
confirmed.failure: A screen-reader user tabbing (or reading in document order with the screen off) through the metrics band after generating a graph hears, for the quality metric: the digits (e.g. '82') then 'everyone's well-linked for 4 buddies each' — with no announcement anywhere of the word 'percent', 'quality', or the Moore-bound explanation a sighted user can get by hovering the gauge. Contrast with the two neighboring metrics on the same panel, `aspl` and `diameter`, each of which pairs its number with an explicit label ('avg hops between any two people', 'most steps between anyone') in the accessible tree.
confirmed.remediation: Move the explanatory sentence (or a shorter equivalent, e.g. `${q}% connection quality — how close to the theoretical best for this many buddies`) into an `aria-label` on the `.gauge` div (or a visually-hidden text node inside it) so it is present in the accessible tree unconditionally, the same way `aspl`/`diameter` already pair their digits with a text label; keep `title` for the mouse tooltip if desired, but don't make it the only channel.
confirmed.invariant: Every piece of information exposed via a `title` attribute on a non-focusable element must also be reachable via the accessible name, accessible description, or an adjacent static/live text node of that element — i.e. no user-facing explanation should be reachable by pointer hover alone.

plausible.theme: a guard is justified in a comment by a sequence I could not construct, so the comment asserts a live hazard the code's own structure appears to exclude
plausible.summary: The comment above the `selected` range clamp says a selection can survive into a shorter replacement view because `resetSelection` runs before the asynchronous `bg.generate`; I could not produce that window, and deleting the clamp passes the suite.
plausible.failure: Seeded mutation: `const selected = rawSelected;` (dropping `&& rawSelected < view.names.length`) → 315 passed. Tracing the three graph-replacing paths, `resetSelection()` and the dispatch are in one React commit (`handleGenerate`, `handleReroll`, and `applyImported` — the last after an `await`, which React 19 still batches), so `explorer.current` is null from the next render onward, and `#app` is `inert` for the whole "running" window, so no new selection can be made before the shorter view lands. I could not construct the sequence the comment describes. I am filing this as PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED because failing to construct it is not proof it is unreachable, and the guard is cheap — the argument is about the comment asserting a mechanism, not about removing the clamp.
plausible.remediation: Either demonstrate the window with a render test (which would also retire the mutation gap), or reword the comment to state what is actually true — that the index is defended because `PersonPanel` hands it to `eccentricity`, whose vertex guard throws and whose throw has no error boundary above it — and drop the causal story about the async dispatch. Do not remove the clamp.
plausible.invariant: In every commit App produces, `explorer.current === null || (view !== null && explorer.current < view.names.length)` — checkable by a render test that selects a high index and then generates/imports a shorter roster.
